linkedin.hook: Shared collateral pools hide systemic tail risk. Isolated balance sheet architecture fixes it.
linkedin.copy:
EVM lending protocols still rely on monolithic pooled liquidity designs established half a decade ago. When market volatility spikes, solvent trading desks end up paying for delayed liquidations through protocol bad debt and cascading slippage. For quantitative teams running automated basis trades, unpredictable rollup priority fees can turn an active position cash-negative in seconds.

Soroban provides a pragmatic runtime for credit primitives because execution costs remain predictable. Vanna Protocol separates balance sheets entirely instead of dumping deposits into a shared liquidity sink. Each trader operates an isolated SmartAccount with a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor. Because invocations run at 0.00014 XLM fixed gas alongside ~320ms Mercury indexer latency, off-chain risk engines can monitor liquidations without getting priced out during high-throughput events.

Institutional credit infrastructure requires deterministic execution, not subsidized liquidity pools that freeze during stress tests. The contracts are live on testnet for quantitative developers and credit funds testing cross-ecosystem capital routing. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance to evaluate execution latency directly.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: Migrating from EVM to Soroban: Building isolated credit accounts without pooled insolvency risk
reddit.copy:
If you have spent the last few years auditing or building on Solidity lending markets, you know the core architectural vulnerability: pooled risk. One bad oracle update or slow liquidation liquidates the collective pool balance.

When we started architecting Vanna Protocol, we moved away from the EVM paradigm to build natively on Stellar's Soroban. The goal was simple: deterministic execution and isolated balance sheets for leveraged yield strategies.

Instead of users depositing into a shared contract that commingles risk, each user deploys an isolated SmartAccount sandbox. Your collateral stays isolated to your address. The contract enforces a 1.10x Health Factor floor directly on-chain, eliminating socialized bad debt across unrelated trading desks.

From an infrastructure perspective, the performance metrics change how bots can interface with the protocol:

Transaction costs are deterministic at roughly 0.00014 XLM per invocation. You do not deal with gas bidding wars during liquidation windows.

Event ingestion via the Mercury indexer runs at ~320ms latency. This allows off-chain risk engines to track position health and trigger adjustments without waiting for multiple rollup block confirmations.

State storage in Soroban requires manual TTL management, which forced us to design ultra-lean state trees for borrower positions rather than bloated EVM mappings.

Testnet is live. We want EVM developers and quants to break the contract math, evaluate liquidation thresholds, and stress-test the isolated accounts. You can deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Disclosure: I am a core engineer at Vanna Protocol. Happy to answer any technical questions about our Soroban Rust contracts, oracle configurations, or risk models in the comments.
